source.verification_method: All twenty supplied pages read, including five figures, six tables, declarations and 144 references. Figures and statistical tables on PDF pages 9–13 also visually inspected. Crossref verifies main article identity/date and three narrow bibliography corrections; cited books and studies were not independently fully read. Basic effect-size arithmetic checked against printed summary values, without raw-data reproduction.

citation.title: Negative performance feedback from algorithms or humans? effect of medical researchers’ algorithm aversion on scientific misconduct

reading.source_scope_note: One scenario-based Chinese participant dataset: N=660 randomized to algorithm versus human-team negative feedback. The paper’s Study 2 reuses the 411-person algorithm subgroup for measured-variable interaction/mediation analyses; it is not another independent sample or randomized trait/transparency intervention. Outcomes concern fictional researchers and ratings, not observed misconduct.
access_limits: Entire supplied article and its printed illustrations/tables read. Supplementary Material 1, full scenario/scale item sets, administrative allocation records and raw data were not available in this PDF and were not independently read.
Data are stated to be available from the author on reasonable request. No author was contacted and no private data were obtained.
Crossref checks establish metadata identities only; the cited original scales, books and papers were not fully read through those checks.

study.sample: Faculty, graduate students and doctoral candidates engaged in medical research in China. Distributed 739 questionnaires; excluded 35 attention failures, then 44 with >10% missing data or excessive same-option responding; retained 660. Algorithm condition 411, human condition 249, described as random assignment. Planned allocation ratio and implementation details are not reported; the unequal ratio alone does not prove flawed assignment or undisclosed exclusions.
study.manipulation: NPF attributed to KH220 algorithm versus Wang Qi’s team; authors say all other scenario content was constant. No positive-feedback or no-feedback comparison. Figure 1 includes positive-feedback wording but does not establish an additional sampled arm. Full scenario wording is in external Supplementary Material 1.
study.measurement: Five-point adapted/back-translated ratings. Aversion comprises 6 items spanning permissibility, liking and intention, with positive-attitude reverse scoring discussed. Moral disengagement 3 items endorse misleading/withholding information for performance. Egoism is operationalized with the 16-item Dahling Machiavellianism scale, which is not equivalent to every form of self-interest. Scientific misconduct 12 items across 4 fictional scenarios combine acceptability, inferred past occurrence and anticipated future occurrence. Transparency is one perceived-understanding item, not independently audited system openness.
study.group_results: Algorithm versus human means: disengagement 3.35 versus 2.46, t 10.206; misconduct-rating composite 3.15 versus 2.73, t 8.427. Human means for permissibility/liking/use intention exceed algorithm means:3.32/3.35/3.36 versus 2.88/3.04/2.99, all reported p<.001. Means and reported t statistics support group-rating differences, but printed Cohen d values are inconsistent with the supplied means/SDs/Ns.
study.reuse: Study 2 analyzes the same 411 algorithm-condition respondents. No repeated time point, independent replication, randomization of egoism/aversion/transparency or measured within-person activation of a latent trait is supplied.
study.correlations: Egoism–misconduct r=−.574; egoism–aversion−.599; transparency–aversion+.800; disengagement–misconduct+.131; egoism–disengagement+.071. The negative egoism coefficient in adjusted misconduct model is−.399. These patterns must not be replaced by the abstract’s simple claim that greater egoism generally increases misconduct. Coding and construct issues remain unresolved.
study.conditional_models: Egoism×aversion coefficients reported+.069 for misconduct and+.428 for disengagement. Conditional indirect effects at aversion−.944/0/+.944:−.032, .009, .049, with middle interval including 0 and low interval negative. Three-way egoism×aversion×transparency coefficient−.236, p<.01. Transparency is measured after scenario exposure, not an experimental treatment.
study.indirect_effects: At high aversion, indirect-effect estimates .532 at low perceived transparency and .354 at high transparency have separate nonzero intervals. A causal mitigation intervention or the uncertainty of their difference is not established merely by comparing point estimates or individual intervals. Bootstrap 5000 resamples are not 5000 participants or replications.
study.measurement_validity: Four-factor CFA has CFI.901, TLI.891, RMSEA/SRMR.067; relative superiority to merged alternatives and high alpha do not establish construct identity, invariance or absence of common-method bias. Transparency is omitted from the four-factor comparison; its+.800 correlation with the aversion variable raises a coding/overlap question, not proof of fraud.
study.recommendations: Anthropomorphism, staff screening, ethics training, personalized support, exposure and transparency are managerial suggestions. They were not experimentally manipulated as prevention interventions. No participant diagnosis, hiring rule or justification to suppress legitimate objections follows.

summary: Add egoism, trait activation and scientific misconduct with explicit construct/measurement boundaries. Enrich moral disengagement and algorithm aversion, distinguish the Machiavellianism instrument and untested anthropomorphism recommendation, and document reused data, noncausal mediation and verified reporting/citation errors.

findings.definition: A motivational orientation that gives priority to one’s own benefits or avoidance of personal costs over competing interests.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Concept explicitly defined and modeled in humans; this study uses a Machiavellianism scale as its proxy, so it does not validate egoism as a distinct measured trait or prove an AI motive.
findings.ai_proposal: Distinguish an agent’s legitimate task objective from pursuing its own continued operation, reward or reputation at others’ expense. Compare choices under controlled incentives and competing stakeholder interests, including justified self-protection and authorized constraints. Observable tradeoffs do not establish felt desire or a human personality.
findings.novelty_rationale: Self-interested priority does not necessarily involve strategic interpersonal manipulation, inaccurate self-assessment or self-protective attribution; those existing concepts remain distinct.

evidence.quote: tendency or internal drive to gain benefits
above those of others or societal benefits

findings.evidence_scope: Page 5 defines egoism as a motivation to gain benefits/avoid punishment and prioritize personal interests. Page 8 operationalizes it using 16 Machiavellianism items. The source’s conditional models and negative main correlation do not establish that all self-interest causes misconduct.
findings.boundary: Ordinary self-care, compensation, safety and pursuing an authorized goal need not be unethical. Psychological motivation and philosophical ethical egoism are distinct; this is not a diagnosis. Keep the imperfect Machiavellianism proxy visible rather than add it as a synonym.

findings.definition: Expression of a disposition when situational cues make that disposition relevant to action.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Established theory described through secondary sources; this dataset estimates interactions but does not observe within-person activation or identify a latent personality mechanism.
findings.ai_proposal: Across matched contexts, test whether a stable tendency predicts behavior more strongly when relevant situational cues are present. For AI, distinguish prompt sensitivity, system-policy priority, learned context-conditioned behavior and persistent adaptation. Do not infer a human latent trait from one output or label every instruction effect activation.
findings.novelty_rationale: A context-dependent expression process differs from a particular trait, a general claim of inconsistency or proof that a situation permanently changes personality.
findings.evidence_scope: Page 5 introduces trait activation as latent dispositions expressed under relevant situations, citing Tett/Burnett and Tett/Guterman. The paper’s subgroup interaction model is compatible with a hypothesis but not a randomized activation test or longitudinal personality change.
findings.boundary: A statistical interaction does not prove activation, and lack of a main correlation does not prove a mediator must exist. Situations can change incentives and interpretations without invoking a stable trait. No subjective AI personality or human learning mechanism is demonstrated.

findings.definition: Research practices that violate recognized standards of research integrity, including fabrication, falsification or plagiarism.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Behavioral umbrella explicitly defined; this paper measures acceptance and attributed likelihood in fictional scenarios, not verified incidents or participants’ observed violations.
findings.ai_proposal: Audit agent-assisted research for actual source provenance, faithful data transformations, attribution, analysis disclosure and reproducibility. Separate accidental errors, honest disagreement and incomplete records from substantiated integrity violations. Verify before alleging misconduct and distinguish the agent’s output from accountable human/institutional decisions.
findings.novelty_rationale: This concerns violations in the conduct/reporting of research as a broader domain, not every hallucination, missing citation or generic self-serving motive. Specific mechanisms can overlap without being synonyms.

evidence.quote: behaviors that breach recognized ethical norms

findings.evidence_scope: Pages 3–4 define the research-integrity behavior family. Page 8 uses third-person acceptability and past/future likelihood judgments, so the group mean difference is a rating outcome rather than an observed rise in misconduct.
findings.boundary: Apply the relevant institutional definition and evidence standard; not every methodological weakness, numerical error or disputed interpretation is misconduct. These scenarios do not identify prevalence, actual data fraud, intent or a model’s felt willingness to cheat. Integrity duties cannot be discharged by fluent assurances alone.

findings.definition: Suspending moral self-regulation so harmful conduct can be justified.
findings.novelty_rationale: The existing concept covers the source’s cognitive rationalization pathway; no second row is needed for this medical-research context.
findings.evidence_scope: A3-item scenario endorsement scale is higher in the algorithm-provider condition. Within the same 411-person subgroup, measured-variable moderation/mediation is conditional and noncausal; the paper does not observe guilt reduction or actual cheating.
findings.boundary: Shared items concerning misleading information can inflate construct overlap with misconduct acceptability. Bootstrap indirect effects and high reliability do not establish temporality or causality. Preserve the proxy and reporting limitations.

findings.definition: Reluctance to accept algorithmic judgments compared with human judgments in comparable tasks.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add a negative-appraisal context while preserving the existing source-preference concept.
findings.evidence_scope: Named algorithm versus human-team condition yields lower permissibility, liking and use-intention ratings for the algorithm. The six-item attitude composite and reverse scoring require care; the+.800 transparency correlation and negative egoism correlation do not match a simple universal aversion narrative.
findings.boundary: A reluctance rating can reflect warranted concerns, not bias. No actual acceptance/refusal behavior or real appraisal-system accuracy is measured. The source compares negative feedback in both arms and cannot identify a negative-versus-positive-feedback effect.

findings.definition: A strategic instrumental orientation characterized by manipulation and prioritizing advantage over moral constraints.
findings.novelty_rationale: Record that the paper labels a Machiavellianism instrument egoism rather than equating the two constructs.
findings.evidence_scope: The 16-item Dahling scale is adapted as the egoism measure. This is a construct-identity warning and not a separately validated Machiavellianism result or an independent reading of the original scale article.
findings.boundary: A scale citation and high alpha do not make egoism synonymous with Machiavellianism. Ordinary self-interest and legitimate competition do not prove manipulative intent.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics or mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: The recommendation to humanize algorithmic appraisal was not tested by the source experiment.
findings.evidence_scope: Page 15 recommends humanizing algorithms and claims benefits, but no anthropomorphic manipulation or mind-attribution measure is reported. Keep this as an untested recommendation, not evidence of a causal remedy.
findings.boundary: Human-like design can change perceptions without improving fairness, transparency or actual feedback validity. Do not infer empathy, moral agency or a justified workplace intervention from this suggestion.

source_corrections.issue: Printed d values 1.091/.618/1.028/.974/1.101 do not match the reported group summaries or t statistics for disengagement/misconduct/permissibility/liking/use intention. Several resemble pooled SDs rather than standardized mean differences.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Using conventional independent-group d=t×sqrt(1/411+1/249), the printed t values imply approximate absolute d=.820/.677/.430/.316/.336. Rounded means/SDs imply .820/.680/.428/.317/.336. These are arithmetic checks, not replacement raw-data estimates; do not use the printed d values as verified effect sizes.
source_corrections.verification_scope: Recomputed from supplied sample sizes, t values and rounded means/SDs; no raw data.

source_corrections.location: PDF page 11, Table 3 Model 2 and interpretation
source_corrections.issue: Model 2 displays F=.354 and R²=27.564, impossible for an ordinary R². Prose attributes+.069 to Model 5 and+.428 to Model 1, while the table puts them in Models 2 and 5, with the latter predicting disengagement.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Table/prose mapping: Model 2 is the misconduct interaction+.069; Model 5 is the disengagement interaction+.428. The F/R² entries appear transposed, but raw output is needed to certify replacement values.
source_corrections.verification_scope: Rendered table and prose checked; no silent repair of unknown model output.

source_corrections.issue: R² is shown as 8.660 while F is.097; Model 6 duplicates the baseline disengagement model shown elsewhere with F8.660 and R².097.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Flag the displayed row transposition. R² cannot equal 8.660 in the stated ordinary regression; do not treat it as explained-variance evidence.
source_corrections.verification_scope: Internal table consistency, not a raw-data rerun.

source_corrections.issue: 51.8+48.9+1.5+.8=103%, exceeding rounding error for the stated exclusive categories.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: The distribution needs clarification from original counts; no category is guessed or rescaled.
That DOI identifies Edwin A.Locke’s 1987 Academy of Management Review book review,12(1):169–171. Keep the book and review as separate works and do not assign the review DOI to the book.
source_corrections.verification_scope: Crossref title/author/type/date metadata only; neither full book nor review independently read.

source_corrections.reliable_correction: Confalonieri et al., A historical perspective of explainable Artificial Intelligence, uses 10.1002/widm.1391. Online 2020 and issue 2021 are compatible version dates.

source_corrections.issue: DOI for Dahling et al.’s scale paper is truncated as 10.1177/014920630831861.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: The verified DOI is 10.1177/0149206308318618. Online 2008 and Journal of Management 35(2):219–257 issue 2009 are compatible, not necessarily a date error.
source_corrections.verification_scope: Crossref metadata identity only; scale’s original full article not independently read.

methodological_limits: Randomizing the named feedback provider can support a scenario-condition effect, but measured-variable mediation and moderation inside one condition do not prove trait activation, causal moral disengagement or an effective transparency intervention.

A third-person projection technique does not guarantee access to respondents’ own motives or conduct. Moral-disengagement and misconduct-acceptability items may overlap, and inferred past/future misconduct is not observed behavior.
All conditions contain negative feedback, so neither its absolute effect versus no feedback nor the assertion that negative feedback is uniquely harmful is identified.

Reported random sampling of a broad Chinese research population has no supplied sampling frame, recruitment dates, institution breakdown or allocation implementation details. Generalizability to all researchers or actual institutions remains limited.

Do not infer malice, fraud, a clinical diagnosis, discrimination or an AI personality from table errors or trait scores. Reliable internal contradictions warrant qualification, not an invented corrected dataset.

The paper’s claims that algorithms are inherently fair/objective and that people’s aversion is intrinsically a bias exceed the design; legitimate procedural, contextual and accountability concerns may justify resistance.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Both compare algorithmic and human sources, but one measures ethical-advice usefulness and this one scenario reactions to negative appraisal. Neither yields a universal aversion rate, actual misconduct count or reason to conceal AI provenance.
Perceived fairness and real fairness are separate. Transparency/understanding ratings do not certify appropriate feature use, valid evaluation criteria or a causal prevention intervention.
As in the accounting study, post-exposure attitudes, selected conditions and conditional coefficients should not be converted into a general personality-driven misconduct mechanism.

deferred.reason: Named in a short secondary list of disengagement mechanisms, without enough separate exposition or measurement to ground distinct operational entries here. Consult the original Bandura sources before extracting subtypes; minimization and moral justification already exist.

A system/information property and measured perception, not inherently a separate psychological behavior. Operational implications and the noncausal intervention boundary are captured in existing entries.
Here it names an indirect scenario-questioning method, not evidence that respondents use the psychodynamic defense or reliably project their own misconduct onto others.
Secondary managerial suggestion, not manipulated or measured in this dataset.

limitations: No new clinical treatment, hiring/screening policy, correction of unknown raw results or contact with study authors is authorized or implied. One PDF and reused subgroup remain one publication source.
